observations: Photo 0, 1, 2 show the same black Yamaha home keyboard, approx 49 mini/full keys, laid on an artificial grass backdrop.
Brand name 'YAMAHA' and partial text 'PortaSound' are visible on the lower-left of the keyboard in photo 2, but the specific model number is not legible in any photo.
Control panel has sliders, small buttons, and a basic LCD-style display typical of late-1980s/1990s entry-level Yamaha keyboards (PSS/PortaSound family), not a modern PSR-series layout.
No power adapter is visible in any photo.
No shot of the back, battery compartment, or underside is provided.
No video or audio evidence of the keyboard powering on or producing sound.
Watermarks 'POSTED ON JIJI' and 'MARY OLUGBAMI' overlay the images; no other text or serial plate is readable.

claims.claim: Quality and good Yamaha keyboard for children
claims.evidence: No usage or condition test shown beyond static photos.
No video or audio of keys being pressed; photos only show the instrument at rest.
No adapter visible in any of the 3 photos.
No proof of purchase, import sticker, or UK plug visible.
Cannot be confirmed from still photos; requires audio/video test.

risks.risk: Keys or buttons may be unresponsive or produce no sound
risks.proof: A video of the seller powering on the keyboard and pressing multiple keys across the range, with audible sound

risks.risk: Adapter may not actually be included or may be wrong voltage/non-original
risks.proof: A clear photo of the adapter next to the keyboard showing plug type and rating
risks.if_unproven: priced as if adapter not included

risks.risk: Hidden cosmetic or structural damage (cracks, battery corrosion, missing feet)
risks.proof: Photos of the back, underside, and battery compartment

risks.risk: Model may be a very low-end/older unit with limited features, affecting resale value
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the model number plate

proof_requests: Video of keyboard powered on, playing keys across full range with sound audible
Clear photo of the model number/serial plate
Photo of the adapter itself (plug, cable, rating label)
Photo of the back/underside of the keyboard
response.reason: The item is clearly a basic vintage Yamaha home/children's keyboard by type, but the model number is unreadable and all functional claims (working keys, adapter, no crackle) are unverified from photos alone, so it must be priced at worst case against comparable basic Yamaha keyboards of similar vintage and condition in the Abuja/Lagos market.
